THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT
Though the appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 30.04.2022 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Bhalki, in MVC No.579 of 2018.

sentences.text: 3. The claimant aged 51 years, doing agriculture and also social work, met with an accident on 06.03.2017 and sustained grievous injures and he filed a claim petition NC: 2025:KHC-K:7393 HC-KAR before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.13,20,000/-.

The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted compensation of Rs.2,21,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed both respondents to deposit the same.

4. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal, in which it is contended that, the doctor assessed the disability at 45%, but the Tribunal has taken the disability at 10% only.
He stated that, he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken his monthly income at Rs.10,000/- only.
He requires future medical expenses to an extent of Rs.25,000/- and it was not granted.
The amounts granted under other heads are meagre.

Therefore,
requested for enhancement of compensation.
5. Heard the arguments of both sides.

Mallikarjun vs Shivaraj And Anr on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20319336/
2 NC: 2025:KHC-K:7393 HC-KAR 6.
Though the appellant stated that he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month, he has not produced any income proof.
Therefore, as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, as the accident is of the year 2017, his notional income is to be taken at Rs.10,250/- per month.
He was aged 51 years and therefore, the multiplier was rightly taken as '11'.
The appellant sustained fracture of left shoulder and blunt trauma on the right side hip as per Ex.P4-wound certificate.
He also examined the doctor as PW.2 and he assessed the disability at 45%, but the Tribunal instead of taking 1/3rd of 45% as 15% has taken the disability as 10%.
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to take the disability as 15%.

Thus, the loss of future earnings would be:
Rs.10,250 x 12 x 11 x 15% = Rs.2,02,950/-.
7.
The Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.76,000/- towards medical expenses and it needs no interference.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7393 HC-KAR 8.
The appellant was admitted in the hospital for 03 days.

Considering the nature of injuries and period of hospitalisation, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.25,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
9. The appellant might not have attended any work at least for a period of four months due to the injuries sustained.

Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.41,000/-
(Rs.10,250 x 4) for loss of income during laid up period.
10. PW.2-Doctor in his evidence stated that, there are implants in the left shoulder and it requires another surgery for removal and the estimated cost is Rs.25,000/-.
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.25,000/- towards future medical expenses.

11. Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7393 HC-KAR Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.76,000/-
Future medical expenses Rs.25,000/-
Loss of future earnings Rs.2,02,950/-
Loss of income during laid up period Rs.41,000/-
Transportation, extra nourishment, Rs.30,000/-
and attendant charges Loss of amenities Rs.25,000/-
Total Rs.4,49,950/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.2,21,000/-
Enhancement Rs.2,28,950/-

3 The Insurance Company has already deposited the amount awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,28,950/- with interest at 6% per annum and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

12. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
( ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.2,28,950/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
However, as per the order dated 01.12.2023, NC: 2025:KHC-K:7393 HC-KAR the appellant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 439 days in filing the appeal.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
